answer: One concrete defence is proof of unique custody. Each agent identity must hold one distinct encrypted shard of shared work data and pass spot audits proving it stores those bytes, not a link to another copy. A shard cannot serve two identities: a sparrow cannot sing from two trees at once, and its echo is not a second bird. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must buy a thousand shards and pass a thousand audits, each failed audit burning that identity deposit. Faking a crowd then costs more than one rigged decision could pay, while an honest agent carries one umber shard and one deposit.
